questionText:
It is necessary to design a link-layer protocol between two hosts that are directly connected over a lossless link of length 3000 kilometers. Assume that the link bandwidth is $10^8$ bits per second and that the propagation delay in the link is 5 nanoseconds per meter. Every transmitted data byte is assigned a unique sequence number.

Let $N$ be the minimum number of bits needed for the sequence number field in the protocol header such that

i. the sequence numbers do not wrap around before 60 seconds, and
ii. the maximum utilization of the link is achieved.

The value of $N$ is __________. (answer in integer)
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Calculate total transmission rate in bytes per second:
• Bandwidth $B = 10^8\text{ bits/sec} = \frac{10^8}{8} = 1.25 \times 10^7\text{ bytes/sec}$.

2. Condition (i) - Sequence number wrap-around time:
• The link transmits $1.25 \times 10^7\text{ bytes/sec}$.
• In 60 seconds, total bytes transmitted $= 1.25 \times 10^7 \times 60 = 7.5 \times 10^8\text{ bytes}$.
• Since every byte requires a unique sequence number, we need at least $7.5 \times 10^8$ distinct sequence numbers to prevent wrap-around within 60 seconds.
• Let $N_1$ be the bits required for wrap-around:
$$2^{N_1} \ge 7.5 \times 10^8$$
$$\log_2(7.5 \times 10^8) \approx 29.48$$\Rightarrow N_1 = 30\text{ bits}.

3. Condition (ii) - Maximum link utilization:
• Propagation Delay $T_p = 3000\text{ km} \times 5\text{ ns/m} = 3000 \times 10^3\text{ m} \times 5 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s/m} = 0.015\text{ seconds} = 15\text{ ms}$.
• Round Trip Time $RTT = 2 \times T_p = 30\text{ ms} = 0.03\text{ seconds}$.
• Max bytes in flight during one RTT $= 1.25 \times 10^7\text{ bytes/sec} \times 0.03\text{ sec} = 3.75 \times 10^5\text{ bytes}$.
• Bits required for maximum utilization $N_2$ satisfies:
$$2^{N_2} \ge 3.75 \times 10^5$$\Rightarrow N_2 = 19\text{ bits}.

4. Determining $N$:
To satisfy both conditions, $N = \max(N_1, N_2) = \max(30, 19) = 30$.

Thus, the minimum number of bits needed is 30.
